blocks.text: JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Ehud. Struck down Eglon of Moab; the land had rest eighty years.
LED ISRAELi
Not given Not given; after the victory "the land had rest fourscore years"
TRIBE
Benjamin
IN THE LINE
4th of 15
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“The LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded.”
PROPHETS
None named
THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
THE CYCLE
Forgetting, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, rest
1 · FORGOT GOD "The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD." Judges 3:12
2 · OPPRESSED: EGLON, KING OF MOAB, 18 YEARS With Ammon and Amalek, Eglon took "the city of palm trees", and Israel served him eighteen years. Judges 3:12–14
3 · CRIED OUT "When the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised them up a deliverer." Judges 3:15
4 · DELIVERED Ehud killed Eglon, then led Israel down from mount Ephraim, held the fords of the Jordan and killed about ten thousand Moabites. Judges 3:21–29
5 · REST The land had rest 80 years. Judges 3:30
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"The LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded." Judges 3:15
To Eglon he said: "I have a message from God unto thee." Judges 3:20
To Israel: "Follow after me: for the LORD hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand." Judges 3:28
"So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel." Judges 3:30

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
Eighteen years of oppression and eighty of rest (Judges 3:14, 3:30). No year BC is given.
Some periods overlap
Sebastian Schmid (1684), Keil (1865), Ewald and Hengstenberg, as listed by Moore; Mack in the ISBE (1915)

Judges 10:7 sells Israel to the Philistines and the Ammonites together, so the two oppressions can run at the same time; Samson judged "in the days of the Philistines". On Keil's reckoning the totals then fit 1 Kings 6:1. Mack also makes Ibzan, Elon and Abdon partly overlap Jephthah and Samson.[1][19][30]
A scheme of forty-year generations
Moore (1895), following Nöldeke (1869) and Wellhausen
Moore notes how often 40, 80 and 20 recur and reads 1 Kings 6:1's 480 years as twelve generations of forty, a systematic chronology in which years of foreign rule are not counted.[19]
A much shorter period
Lepsius and Bunsen, as reported by Keil
Starting from the view that the numbers are round, Lepsius and Bunsen held that the whole period lasted only 169 to 187 years. Keil reports this in order to reject it.[1]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 2
Judges 3 Judges 4
PASSAGES · 2
Judges 3:12–30 Judges 4:1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Judges calls Ehud a "deliverer" (3:15) but never says that he "judged Israel".
Scripture does not say what Ehud did during the eighty years of rest; the next notice is "when Ehud was dead" (Judges 4:1).
Shamgar, who "also delivered Israel" with an ox goad after Ehud (Judges 3:31), is not given a page here: the text never says he judged.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThe site's family data, from STEP Bible, links "Gera" to the son of Benjamin in Genesis 46:21 and attaches the "sons of Ehud" of 1 Chronicles 8:6 to this Ehud. Judges states neither link. Judges 3:15 Genesis 46:21 1 Chronicles 8:6
